decisions.summary: one review tree per clone (<clone>-review) with its own cargo target and its own .gencache, added once then reset each run and kept, never piled up (9.3 GB, 64-67 GB free throughout, measured 2026-11-22)
decisions.why: the GM's 2026-11-22 purpose is that disk is not eaten 'without us realizing it'; the tree is bounded to one per clone, reused rather than multiplied, its size measured and stated, and T158's floor and cleanup named as a constraint. Keeping it is what makes the warm gate about a minute rather than a cold build, so keeping is the reuse the GM endorsed, not a departure.

decisions.summary: the review tree does not share the landing target
decisions.why: it stands against the GM's 2026-11-22 'your points about reusing the same build cache and whatnot are well taken' (the session's points themselves are not quoted in the bundle). Ground: measured on a scratch copy, cargo judged l7r_guard Fresh across worktrees whose pair_hooks/review.rs and state.rs differ, so a shared target makes the gate judge other code - applying reuse here would defeat the gate's own purpose and the GM's 2026-11-22 cleanup aim is still met by bounding the tree to one. Reuse is kept where it is sound: the content-keyed rust-checks and hooks-test results are seeded from the clone.

decisions.summary: the clone's 6.2 GB .gencache is no longer seeded into the review tree; the tree keeps its own across resets
decisions.why: also against 'reusing the same build cache' (the session's points not quoted in the bundle). Ground: impossibility, observed - entries are keyed by the engine binary's build id, which embeds the tree's source path, so ids never match across trees; of 31,067 seeded entries none served a map. Removing it removes 19.2 s and 6.2 GB of work that reused nothing, which serves both the cleanup and performance requests.

decisions.summary: reviews prereq and the pair guard judge a snapshotted unit by the review tree's record (gate at its key), every other unit by the clone's stamp as before; agent files read review-paired-gate UNIT=
decisions.why: keeps the review paired with the gate (feature 151) while judging the bundle's own tree; the agent-file fix closes the path by which the incident would recur. Note: the search for bare review-paired-gate callers is stated as grep -rn over .claude/agents, rust/, scripts/ - the Makefile, docs/, tests/, CLAUDE.md and the rest of .claude/ are not shown as searched; a reach gap in the enumeration, not a narrowing.

FR-009's three parts are present: why not here, filed id T165, and its order 'lands before T154'. Deferral to a filed, ordered performance task narrows nothing the GM asked.

decisions.summary: T165 withdrawn as done by T175: a review naming a review tree holds only edits inside it, one naming none and the rolls hold the clone; nothing built.
decisions.why: T165's ask, as the block quotes it, is to narrow the engine freeze to reviews with no review-tree snapshot (and the rolls). The block shows the snapshot and the prompt line T175 keys on are written under one condition (a non-empty --commit), so T175's rule is that ask; it is backed by a measured live case (449 T383's two reviews kept PASS at the tree's key while five rust/ files were edited, no engine-freeze firing since T175 landed against 20 before it, 2026-11-23) and the engine-freeze suite green. Withdrawing a task whose ask is already met drops nothing that was asked.

decisions.summary: review-tree.sh carries its bundle to reviews owed --check-declared by L7R_VERIFY_STARTED, read in place of the clone's shared active-task mark; a gate built before reads the mark as before; no feature dir or no task falls back to the mark's rule.
decisions.why: The measurement restates T166's cause (the shared mark moved by another session's set-down or task-start, not a worktree lacking the mark) and the fix targets that cause, so verify judges the bundle it verifies. The environment-variable route and the fallbacks preserve existing behavior for old gates and undeclared cases; nothing the task asked for is dropped. Pinned red-first by a crate test and a suite case.

decisions.summary: Of the carried bundle, only the FIRST task counts as the started one (a CONVENTION); a declared line naming only the bundle's second task is refused.
decisions.why: The first-task rule already exists: make task-start marks a bundle by its first task, 449 T238 round 2 answers a line naming the started task, and the landing's holding box reads the same. T166 changes WHERE the started task is read from (the carried bundle, not the shared mark), not WHICH task counts; neither request.md nor FR-013 says which of a bundle's tasks answers. The block's 'algorithmically easier' remark is not the ground for this class - the ground is that verify and the landing keep one rule, so verify does not pass what the landing then refuses.

The request's purpose, accurate per-task time, is still carried.

decisions.why: The observed failure is recorded with its commit, load and method; the measurements of the failed reproductions are labeled; the fix is the one whose mechanism removes the cause. Settles how the defect is shown, narrows nothing.

decisions.why: It narrows the plan's own class by one instance, but editing a file another builder holds mid-edit in the same shared clone is the very collision T161 exists to stop (one builder's landing claiming or refusing another's files); the defect is not dropped but filed with its id, its reason and its order ahead of T159 (FR-009). No GM words ask for this instance to land in this task, and the request's purpose (bundled small fixes that land without tripping each other, T141) is served, not gutted, by the deferral.

decisions.summary: T161: filed.rs' task chain gains, after the brief's own words, the agent's builder reading (builder_brief: description head, else the prompt's first line, a bundle's every member, else the parentAgentId builder), then a page session's brief (page_session_brief moved to set_down_hooks, one reader); renumbered's briefed reads the builder reading too
decisions.why: Extends where a line's task is found so each agent's line is booked to the task its own dispatch names - FR-004's 'its task where its dispatch names one' and the per-task breakdown the GM asked for (2026-11-19). The move to one reader is a refactor.

decisions.summary: T161: D2's last rung (a line naming no task takes the feature's task-start in force) read for the main session's own lines alone; an agent's or page session's line naming no task carries none (land-alone's and closing checks' splits leave it unnamed, context_cap_hooks names the handoff <agent>.md)
decisions.why: It narrows the accepted spec's D2, which gives every line the clone's task-start in force. Applied literally D2 defeats the request's own purpose, concretely: the GM asked for 'for each task ... a breakdown of where our time went on that task', and D2's last rung booked a sheet-bundle builder's four edits to T317, another builder's task, and so refused a CLEAR, committed bundle at its landing (measured 2026-11-22 from the real log line and meta file). The spec's own FR-004 already limits an agent's line to 'its task where its dispatch names one'; a line with no task is honest where D2's would be wrong. The main session keeps the rung, where the mark is its own.

Removing it removes 19.2 s and 6.2 GB of work that reused nothing, which serves both the cleanup and performance requests.
